description: Legacy screenshots are pushed straight to storage by the CLI and registered against a route, state and viewport the project declared. The first legacy shot for a coordinate is pinned as the baseline; an undeclared state or resolution is refused before any bytes move; and the pinned shot is visible against its route on the project screen.

model.description: The baseline side: the named states a screen can be captured in, the rebuild branches a shot can belong to instead of legacy, and the shot rows themselves. Every part of a shot's claim is a foreign key, so nothing can be uploaded against a state, resolution or branch the project never declared.

items.description: One named condition a screen can be in — a dialog open, a tab selected, a validation error. A state belongs to exactly one route, so a state declared on another screen does not count for this one. `ref` is free text a person reads and diffui never resolves.

One rebuild. Legacy is deliberately NOT one of these: modelling legacy as the branch called legacy would make branch-against-branch expressible, and the moment it is expressible someone scores two rebuilds against each other and calls the winner done. The table lands here because a shot names the side it came from.

One captured PNG and the claim of what it shows. The image bytes live in storage; this row names the key they were written at. `is_baseline` pins WHICH legacy shot everyone is measured against, because legacy still runs and can be recaptured — without it the baseline would drift to whatever landed last.

functions.description: The push, in the three steps images-never-pass-through-the-api requires: ask where to put it, PUT the bytes at storage, register the row. The coordinates are resolved before a URL is handed out, so an undeclared state fails before a byte moves.

items.name: declareBranch
items.description: Declare the rebuild a shot manifest names, upserting it by key, so a rebuild shot has something to belong to.
items.permission: Only someone in the organisation that owns the project may declare a rebuild for it.

items.name: requestShotUpload
items.description: Hand back a short-lived, path-bound upload URL for one screenshot, at storage rather than through the API. The route, state, viewport and side are resolved first, so a coordinate nobody declared is refused here.
items.permission: Only someone in the organisation that owns the project may be handed a place to upload a shot of it.

items.name: registerShot
items.description: Record the captured PNG against the screen, state, resolution and side it is of, reading dimensions from the image rather than trusting the manifest. The first legacy shot for a coordinate takes the baseline role unasked; a later one only displaces it when the push says to re-pin.
items.permission: Only someone in the organisation that owns the project may record a screenshot against it.

items.name: listShots
items.description: A project's shots with the route, state and viewport each belongs to, and which one is pinned as the baseline, so the screen can show a captured shot against its route.
items.permission: Only someone in the organisation that owns the project may see its shots.

roles.description: The same one engineer, on the same app. This milestone adds no person and no frontend — the baseline lands on the screen the previous milestone already gave them.

items.name: engineer
items.description: Runs a rebuild — pushes screenshots from the CLI and reads what landed against each route

scopes.description: No scopes. Pushing a screenshot is gated by organisation membership of the project being pushed to, which depends on the row and is therefore a permission, not a scope. A scope would read the same for every row, and this one does not.

ui.description: The project screen gains the other half of a route: the legacy shot that landed against it, marked when it is the pinned baseline. No new screen — the route list the engineer already reads is where a baseline belongs.

items.description: One project's routes, each showing the legacy baseline shot that has landed against it — the image itself, and a mark saying this is the one every rebuild is measured against.

backend.description: Legacy bytes go straight to storage and the row that points at them is registered; a coordinate nobody declared is refused.

browser.description: Maya pushes a legacy shot and sees it against the route, marked as the baseline — the milestone's own gherkin driven as a person.

permission.description: The push is refused to anyone outside the organisation that owns the project, for every step of it — the URL, the registration, the branch it names and the shots it reads back.
